views.name: hits_explode
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s._TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  s.visitId,
  s.visitStartTime,
  CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.userId,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_number,
  hit.time AS hit_time_seconds,
  hit.hour AS hit_hour,
  hit.minute AS hit_minute,
  hit.type AS hit_type,
  hit.isEntrance AS is_entrance,
  hit.isExit AS is_exit,
  hit.isInteraction AS is_interaction,
  hit.referer AS referer,
  hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
  hit.page.pageTitle AS page_title,
  hit.eventInfo.eventCategory AS event_category,
  hit.eventInfo.eventAction AS event_action,
  hit.eventInfo.eventLabel AS event_label,
  hit.eventInfo.eventValue AS event_value,
  hit.transaction.transactionId AS hit_transaction_id,
  hit.transaction.transactionRevenue AS hit_transaction_revenue,
  hit.item.itemRevenue AS hit_item_revenue,
  hit.social.socialInteractionNetwork AS social_network,
  hit.social.socialInteractionAction AS social_action
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit
grain: one row per hit per session (visitId) per shard (table_suffix)

params.description: One row per Google Analytics hit within a session (visit) for each underlying table shard: exposes hit-level attributes (timing, type, page, event, transaction/item/social fields) for analysis or composition into higher-level aggregates.
params.when_to_use: Analyze hit-level behavior (e.g., distribution of hit types, entrance/exit/interactions, hit timing within sessions). | Drill from session-level summaries down to the individual hits that make up a session. | Compose hit-level counts, sums or time-based metrics into session- or user-level aggregates (after appropriate aggregation). | Join hit-level attributes to exploded product or transaction datasets (careful about duplication) to build item-level revenue views.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: the underlying BigQuery table shard suffix from ga_sessions_* (_TABLE_SUFFIX) which identifies the date-sharded source table (source: s._TABLE_SUFFIX). | session_date: the session date parsed from the source 'date' string in format YYYYMMDD (source: PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date)). | visitId: the session (visit) identifier from the sessions table (source: s.visitId). | visitStartTime: session start timestamp field from sessions (source: s.visitStartTime). | visitor_id: visitorId coerced to STRING; internal visitor identifier from sessions (source: CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING)). | fullVisitorId: fullVisitorId from sessions (source: s.fullVisitorId). | userId: GA userId if set (source: s.userId). | hit_number: the hit sequence number within the session (source: hit.hitNumber). | hit_time_seconds: seconds offset of the hit relative to the session (source: hit.time). | hit_hour: hour of day for the hit (if recorded) (source: hit.hour). | hit_minute: minute of hour for the hit (if recorded) (source: hit.minute). | hit_type: hit.type (PAGE, EVENT, TRANSACTION, SOCIAL, etc.) (source: hit.type). | is_entrance: boolean flag indicating whether the hit is an entrance (source: hit.isEntrance). | is_exit: boolean flag indicating whether the hit is an exit (source: hit.isExit). | is_interaction: boolean flag indicating whether the hit counts as an interaction (source: hit.isInteraction). | referer: referring URL recorded for the hit (source: hit.referer). | page_path: page path for pageview hits (source: hit.page.pagePath). | page_title: page title for pageview hits (source: hit.page.pageTitle). | event_category: eventInfo.eventCategory for event hits (source: hit.eventInfo.eventCategory). | event_action: eventInfo.eventAction for event hits (source: hit.eventInfo.eventAction). | event_label: eventInfo.eventLabel for event hits (source: hit.eventInfo.eventLabel). | event_value: eventInfo.eventValue numeric value for event hits (source: hit.eventInfo.eventValue). | hit_transaction_id: transaction.transactionId associated with this hit (source: hit.transaction.transactionId). | hit_transaction_revenue: transaction.transactionRevenue on this hit (source: hit.transaction.transactionRevenue). | hit_item_revenue: item.itemRevenue on this hit (source: hit.item.itemRevenue). | social_network: social.socialInteractionNetwork for social hits (source: hit.social.socialInteractionNetwork). | social_action: social.socialInteractionAction for social hits (source: hit.social.socialInteractionAction).
params.grounded_columns: s._TABLE_SUFFIX | s.date | s.visitId | s.visitStartTime | s.visitorId | s.fullVisitorId | s.userId | s.hits | hit.hitNumber | hit.time | hit.hour | hit.minute | hit.type | hit.isEntrance | hit.isExit | hit.isInteraction | hit.referer | hit.page.pagePath | hit.page.pageTitle | hit.eventInfo.eventCategory | hit.eventInfo.eventAction | hit.eventInfo.eventLabel | hit.eventInfo.eventValue | hit.transaction.transactionId | hit.transaction.transactionRevenue | hit.item.itemRevenue | hit.social.socialInteractionNetwork | hit.social.socialInteractionAction
params.metric: hit_count = COUNT(*) OVER () when aggregated appropriately per grouping; base view emits one row per hit so hit_count must be produced by COUNT(hit_number) or COUNT(*) after GROUP BY (definition: to count hits, use COUNT(*) on this view grouped by desired key). | sum_hit_time_seconds = SUM(hit_time_seconds) when aggregated per grouping (definition: SUM(hit_time_seconds) after GROUP BY). | sum_event_value = SUM(IFNULL(event_value,0)) when aggregated per grouping (definition: SUM(COALESCE(event_value,0)) after GROUP BY). | sum_hit_transaction_revenue = SUM(IFNULL(hit_transaction_revenue,0)) (definition: SUM(COALESCE(hit_transaction_revenue,0)) after GROUP BY). | sum_hit_item_revenue = SUM(IFNULL(hit_item_revenue,0)) (definition: SUM(COALESCE(hit_item_revenue,0)) after GROUP BY).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to session-level or visitor-level 1:1 views on (table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId) or (table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitStartTime) — safe because this view is one row per hit WITHIN a (table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId) session; joining a 1:1 session-level view will not duplicate hit rows and preserves hit-level measures when the session view has at most one row per session key. | safe to join to daily/session shard dimension tables on (table_suffix, session_date) or (table_suffix, session_date, visitId) if those dimension tables are keyed 1:1 to the same session identifier — they do not duplicate hit rows. | do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child that is at a coarser grain (for example, products_explode or any other item-level exploded table) without re-aggregation, because those joins can multiply rows and thus duplicate sums/counts from this view. Instead either: (a) aggregate hits up to the join key before joining (e.g., GROUP BY table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId to derive session-level metrics), or (b) join on keys that guarantee 1:1 (rare) or (c) perform a proper distinct/first_value reduction on the many-side before join. | do NOT join to sibling products_explode (one-to-many: a session/hit can map to multiple product rows) unless you first aggregate products to the session/hit key or aggregate hits to the product key. Example safe patterns: (a) To compute revenue per hit, aggregate products_explode to (table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId, hit_number) to a single product-level measure before joining to hits_explode; (b) To compute session-level metrics, GROUP BY session keys on hits_explode and products_explode separately, then join aggregated results. | When composing into user/session aggregates (user_session_summary, daily_session_aggregates): aggregate hits_explode by the same session or user key as the target aggregate (e.g., GROUP BY table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId for session metrics; GROUP BY table_suffix, fullVisitorId or fullVisitorId for user metrics) before joining — this avoids row multiplication and preserves correct totals. | If joining to ranked or windowed sibling views (sessions_rank_by_revenue, session_running_totals_by_visitor): ensure the sibling view is at session-level (one row per session) and join on the session key (table_suffix, fullVisitorId, visitId or visitStartTime) which is 1:1; avoid joining to versions of those views that are at a coarser/finer grain without appropriate aggregation.

views.description: One row per hit within a session. Preserves session keys and basic hit attributes (hitNumber, time, type, page, event, transaction) for event-level analysis or aggregation. Useful when attributing pageviews, events, or hit-level timestamps. | Use for: Top pages by pageviews or entrances; Event funnels or event counts by category/action/label; Hit-level time series or session time distribution

views.name: products_explode
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s._TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  s.visitId,
  s.visitStartTime,
  CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  s.fullVisitorId,
  s.userId,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_number,
  prod.productSKU AS product_sku,
  prod.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  prod.v2ProductCategory AS product_category,
  prod.productBrand AS product_brand,
  prod.productPrice AS product_price,
  prod.productRevenue AS product_revenue,
  prod.productQuantity AS product_quantity,
  prod.isImpression AS is_impression,
  prod.isClick AS is_click,
  prod.productListName AS product_list_name,
  prod.productListPosition AS product_list_position
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit,
UNNEST(hit.product) AS prod
grain: one row per product instance within a hit within a session per shard

params.description: Exploded product-level rows for each product instance within a hit within a session (one row per product within a hit per session shard).
params.when_to_use: When you need product-level detail (SKU, name, category, brand, price, quantity, revenue) for every product instance observed in hits. | When composing session- or visitor-level aggregates from product-level data (e.g., total product revenue per session or per visitor) — but ensure correct re-aggregation when joining other one-to-many tables. | When filtering or segmenting product events by hit attributes (hit_number) or session attributes (session_date, visitId, visitor_id, visitStartTime). | When deriving product impression vs click level analyses (is_impression, is_click) per product instance within hits.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: Suffix of the underlying table shard (s._TABLE_SUFFIX). Identifies which ga_sessions_* shard the row came from. | session_date: Parsed date of the session (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date)). | visitId: Session-scoped visit id from the ga_sessions table (s.visitId). | visitStartTime: Session start time from the ga_sessions table (s.visitStartTime). | visitor_id: Visitor id cast to string (CAST(s.visitorId AS STRING)). | fullVisitorId: fullVisitorId from ga_sessions (s.fullVisitorId). | userId: userId from ga_sessions (s.userId). | hit_number: Hit number inside the session (hit.hitNumber). | product_sku: Product SKU from the exploded product structure (prod.productSKU). | product_name: Product name / v2ProductName from the exploded product structure (prod.v2ProductName). | product_category: Product category / v2ProductCategory from the exploded product structure (prod.v2ProductCategory). | product_brand: Product brand (prod.productBrand). | product_price: Product price (prod.productPrice). Numeric as provided by the source product record. | product_revenue: Product revenue (prod.productRevenue). Numeric as provided by the source product record — this typically reflects revenue attributed to this product instance. | product_quantity: Quantity for this product instance (prod.productQuantity). | is_impression: Boolean/flag indicating this product was recorded as an impression on the hit (prod.isImpression). | is_click: Boolean/flag indicating this product was recorded as a click on the hit (prod.isClick). | product_list_name: Product list name (prod.productListName) if the product was part of a list. | product_list_position: Position of the product within the list (prod.productListPosition).
params.grounded_columns: s._TABLE_SUFFIX | s.date | s.visitId | s.visitStartTime | s.visitorId | s.fullVisitorId | s.userId | hit.hitNumber | prod.productSKU | prod.v2ProductName | prod.v2ProductCategory | prod.productBrand | prod.productPrice | prod.productRevenue | prod.productQuantity | prod.isImpression | prod.isClick | prod.productListName | prod.productListPosition
params.metric: product_price = prod.productPrice  -- base numeric field per product instance as emitted by the hit.product element | product_revenue = prod.productRevenue  -- revenue attributed to this product instance in the hit.product element | product_quantity = prod.productQuantity  -- quantity reported on the product entry | derived example: session_product_revenue = SUM(product_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY session_key)  -- not implemented in view, example of how to aggregate product_revenue to session level; session_key = (fullVisitorId, visitStartTime, visitId) or use session_date + visitId depending on downstream joins
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sessions_aggregates-like views on the session key (fullVisitorId + visitStartTime + visitId OR visitId + session_date when visitId unique per day) — safe because products_explode is one row per product instance within a hit within a session, and joining to a single-row-per-session view will not duplicate session-level aggregates when you aggregate product measures after the join. Example: JOIN daily_session_aggregates ON (products_explode.fullVisitorId = daily_session_aggregates.fullVisitorId AND products_explode.visitStartTime = daily_session_aggregates.visitStartTime) — daily_session_aggregates is one-row-per-session so multiplicity is controlled. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hits_explode on the hit-level key (fullVisitorId + visitStartTime + visitId + hit_number) — safe because hits_explode is one-row-per-hit and products_explode is one-row-per-product-in-hit; you should expect a one-to-many relationship from hit -> product (hits_explode row joins to multiple products_explode rows). This does NOT duplicate product-level measures when you keep the product grain; but if you aggregate at the hit-level after joining, re-aggregate product measures appropriately (e.g., SUM(product_revenue) GROUP BY hit key) to avoid double counting. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to other one-to-many tables that expand products_explode's rows (for example, if you have a separate product_attributes_long table keyed only by product_sku that contains multiple rows per SKU, joining it directly will multiply product-level rows). Instead, pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., collapse product_attributes_long to one row per product_sku) or aggregate products_explode back to the desired grain before joining. | do NOT join to transactions_from_hits or any transaction-level table without understanding cardinality: transactions_from_hits is transaction-level and may be one-to-many relative to products_explode if transactions contain multiple products; if joining transaction rows to product rows to compute transaction totals, either (a) join and then aggregate at transaction grain using SUM(product_revenue) GROUP BY transaction_id, or (b) join to a pre-aggregated transaction summary to avoid multiplying product measures. | safe composition patterns: (1) to compute session-level product revenue: SELECT fullVisitorId, visitStartTime, visitId, SUM(product_revenue) AS session_product_revenue FROM products_explode GROUP BY fullVisitorId, visitStartTime, visitId; (2) to attach single-valued session metadata from user_session_summary: JOIN user_session_summary ON (products_explode.fullVisitorId = user_session_summary.fullVisitorId AND products_explode.visitStartTime = user_session_summary.visitStartTime) — safe because user_session_summary is one-row-per-session; (3) to enrich product master attributes: first reduce master to one row per product_sku, then JOIN ON product_sku — safe because you made the master table one-row-per-sku. | reasoning for cardinality rules: this view's grain is product-instance-within-hit-within-session. Any join to a table that is one-row-per-session will not multiply product rows; joins to tables that are one-to-many relative to product-instance (for example, multiple custom dimensions per hit, multiple product attributes per sku, or multiple transactions per session) will multiply rows and measures unless the many-side is pre-aggregated or the downstream query re-aggregates to the target grain.

views.description: One row per product occurrence (product array inside hits). Preserves session and hit identifiers, product attributes and revenue/quantity measures. Use when analyzing product-level revenue, counts, or SKU-level metrics. | Use for: Top products by revenue or quantity; Product list position performance or impression-to-click analysis; SKU-level revenue attribution to sessions/channels

views.name: daily_session_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  geoNetwork.country AS country,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_category,
  COUNT(1) AS sessions,
  SUM(totals.pageviews) AS pageviews,
  SUM(totals.hits) AS hits,
  SUM(totals.transactions) AS transactions,
  SUM(totals.transactionRevenue) AS transaction_revenue,
  SUM(totals.bounces) AS bounces
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
GROUP BY session_date, country, device_category

params.description: Daily aggregated session-level totals (sessions, pageviews, hits, transactions, revenue, bounces) broken down by session_date, country, and device_category.
params.when_to_use: Get daily totals by country and device for trend charts or reporting (e.g., sessions per day per country/device). | Feed as a pre-aggregated input to higher-level aggregates (e.g., weekly/monthly totals) by GROUP BY on session_date or by rolling dates. | Join to dimension tables that are one-row-per-country or one-row-per-device to enrich labels without changing measures. | Compose with other pre-aggregates (for example user-level aggregates) when building multi-grain analyses, provided correct key relationships and re-aggregation are used.
params.output_schema: session_date: DATE - parsed from the source string `date` via PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date); the aggregation grain includes this date. | country: STRING - taken from base column `geoNetwork.country`; identifies the country value used in GROUP BY. | device_category: STRING - taken from base column `device.deviceCategory`; identifies the device category value used in GROUP BY. | sessions: INTEGER - COUNT(1) over rows in the source tables for the grouped keys (represents number of sessions for the (session_date, country, device_category) combination). | pageviews: NUMERIC/INTEGER - SUM(totals.pageviews) aggregated from the base column `totals.pageviews` for the grouped keys. | hits: NUMERIC/INTEGER - SUM(totals.hits) aggregated from the base column `totals.hits` for the grouped keys. | transactions: NUMERIC/INTEGER - SUM(totals.transactions) aggregated from the base column `totals.transactions` for the grouped keys. | transaction_revenue: NUMERIC/INTEGER - SUM(totals.transactionRevenue) aggregated from the base column `totals.transactionRevenue` for the grouped keys. | bounces: NUMERIC/INTEGER - SUM(totals.bounces) aggregated from the base column `totals.bounces` for the grouped keys.
params.grounded_columns: `date` (source string parsed to session_date) referenced in PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) | `geoNetwork.country` | `device.deviceCategory` | `totals.pageviews` | `totals.hits` | `totals.transactions` | `totals.transactionRevenue` | `totals.bounces`
params.metric: sessions = COUNT(1)  -- count of source rows (sessions) per (session_date, country, device_category) | pageviews = SUM(totals.pageviews)  -- sum of pageview counts from each session row per group | hits = SUM(totals.hits)  -- sum of hit counts from each session row per group | transactions = SUM(totals.transactions)  -- sum of transactions reported on each session row per group | transaction_revenue = SUM(totals.transactionRevenue)  -- sum of transactionRevenue on each session row per group | bounces = SUM(totals.bounces)  -- sum of bounce indicators (as provided in totals.bounces) per group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-country dimension on country (e.g., country_dim.country = daily_session_aggregates.country) — safe because this view is one row per (date,country,device) so joining to a country dimension that is one-to-one on country will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-device dimension on device_category (e.g., device_dim.device_category = daily_session_aggregates.device_category) — safe for the same reason as above. | do NOT join directly to hits_explode (NORM) or products_explode (NORM) without re-aggregation: those sibling views expand session-level rows to many hit- or product-level rows. Joining them directly to this aggregated view will multiply this view's measures (pageviews, sessions, etc.). If you need hit- or product-level attributes, either (a) join the base normalized table and then re-aggregate correctly by the aggregate's keys, or (b) aggregate the exploded view up to the same grain (session_date, country, device_category) before joining. | do NOT join to transactions_from_hits (JOIN) or any multi-row-per-session table without re-aggregation: those joins can create one-to-many relationships with sessions and will duplicate summed metrics. Instead, join on keys that guarantee one-to-one (or aggregate the right side to the aggregate's grain first). | when combining with user_session_summary (AGG) or session_running_totals_by_visitor (WIN): ensure you align grains before combining. These sibling aggregates may be at a different grain (e.g., visitor or session rank). To compose, either (a) aggregate this view up or down as appropriate (e.g., sum sessions across device_category to match a visitor-level grain) or (b) join on exact matching keys that preserve one-row-per-key semantics; otherwise re-aggregate after the join. | safe re-aggregation pattern: if you must join a one-to-many detail source to enrich dimensions (e.g., attach product attributes), perform the join at the detail level and then GROUP BY session_date, country, device_category to recompute sessions and sums from the detail rows rather than relying on this view's pre-aggregated measure columns. | keys to use for safe joins: (session_date, country, device_category) is the full grain key. Any join where the other table is strictly one-row-per-(session_date,country,device_category) or one-row-per-country or one-row-per-device is safe; any join where the other table is one-to-many across those keys is unsafe without re-aggregation.

views.description: Daily aggregated session metrics by country and device category. Exposes counts and sums needed for trend analysis and basic KPI dashboards. Use by applying a date-range filter on table_suffix or session_date in downstream queries. | Use for: Daily KPIs by geography and device; Comparing device performance over time; Filtering top-performing countries by revenue or sessions

views.name: user_session_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS first_session_date,
  MAX(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS last_session_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '|', CAST(visitId AS STRING))) AS sessions_count,
  SUM(totals.pageviews) AS total_pageviews,
  SUM(totals.hits) AS total_hits,
  SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions,
  SUM(totals.transactionRevenue) AS total_transaction_revenue,
  AVG(totals.timeOnSite) AS avg_time_on_site
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
GROUP BY fullVisitorId

params.description: Per-visitor (fullVisitorId) session-level summary: first/last session dates, counts and sums of sessions, pageviews, hits, transactions, revenue, and average time on site.
params.when_to_use: Report or analysis that needs one row per visitor summarizing their activity across all sessions in the underlying GA sample tables. | As a building block to compute visitor-level KPIs (e.g., average revenue per visitor, session frequency by cohort) without re-aggregating raw session rows. | Composition when you need to join visitor-level attributes (demographics, custom dimensions) onto aggregated visitor behavior. | Feeding a machine learning feature set that requires per-visitor aggregates rather than per-session or per-hit data.
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: unique visitor identifier (derived directly from the base column fullVisitorId from ga_sessions_*) | first_session_date: earliest session date for the visitor (derived from MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) where date is the ga_sessions_* date string) | last_session_date: latest session date for the visitor (derived from MAX(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) where date is the ga_sessions_* date string) | sessions_count: number of distinct sessions for the visitor (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '|', CAST(visitId AS STRING))) — counts distinct visitId occurrences across sharded tables, using _TABLE_SUFFIX to avoid collisions across partitions) | total_pageviews: sum of totals.pageviews across all sessions for the visitor (derived from SUM(totals.pageviews) from ga_sessions_*) | total_hits: sum of totals.hits across all sessions for the visitor (derived from SUM(totals.hits) from ga_sessions_*) | total_transactions: sum of totals.transactions across all sessions for the visitor (derived from SUM(totals.transactions) from ga_sessions_*) | total_transaction_revenue: sum of totals.transactionRevenue across all sessions for the visitor (derived from SUM(totals.transactionRevenue) from ga_sessions_*) | avg_time_on_site: average per-session totals.timeOnSite for the visitor (derived from AVG(totals.timeOnSite) from ga_sessions_*)
params.grounded_columns: ga_sessions_*.fullVisitorId | ga_sessions_*.date | ga_sessions_*.visitId | ga_sessions_*.totals.pageviews | ga_sessions_*.totals.hits | ga_sessions_*.totals.transactions | ga_sessions_*.totals.transactionRevenue | ga_sessions_*.totals.timeOnSite | _TABLE_SUFFIX (sharded table identifier used in COUNT DISTINCT expression)
params.metric: first_session_date = MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date))  -- earliest session date per fullVisitorId | last_session_date = MAX(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date))  -- latest session date per fullVisitorId | sessions_count = COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '|', CAST(visitId AS STRING)))  -- distinct session count across sharded tables, keyed by visitId plus table suffix | total_pageviews = SUM(totals.pageviews)  -- visitor-level total pageviews (sum of per-session pageviews) | total_hits = SUM(totals.hits)  -- visitor-level total hits (sum of per-session hits) | total_transactions = SUM(totals.transactions)  -- visitor-level total transactions (sum of per-session transactions) | total_transaction_revenue = SUM(totals.transactionRevenue)  -- visitor-level total transaction revenue (sum of per-session transactionRevenue) | avg_time_on_site = AVG(totals.timeOnSite)  -- visitor-level average of per-session timeOnSite
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to visitor-level dimension tables or views (one-row-per-fullVisitorId) on fullVisitorId — safe because user_session_summary is one row per fullVisitorId, so measures will not be duplicated. Example: join to a visitors_demographics view keyed by fullVisitorId. | cardinality-SAFE: join to other AGG-level views that are also one-row-per-fullVisitorId on fullVisitorId — safe for direct joins (e.g., session_running_totals_by_visitor if it is one-row-per-fullVisitorId). | DO NOT join directly to session-level or hit-level tables/views (e.g., ga_sessions_*, hits_explode, products_explode, transactions_from_hits) on fullVisitorId without re-aggregation, because those are one-to-many relative to this view and will multiply counts/sums. Instead, either: (a) aggregate the child table to one row per fullVisitorId before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate after the join ensuring proper DISTINCT/aggregation semantics. | DO NOT join to views that produce multiple rows per visitor (RANK, WIN, or long/reshaped custom_dimensions_long) without reducing them to one row per fullVisitorId first (for example by choosing a single row per visitor or aggregating metrics), because that will duplicate the aggregated measures in this view. | Safe join keys summary: use fullVisitorId as the join key when the other side is guaranteed one-row-per-fullVisitorId. If joining on additional keys (e.g., date or visitId), be aware sessions_count and per-visitor aggregates are computed across all dates/visits — joining on narrower keys will filter rows and change aggregates; joining on visitId requires re-aggregation at session or hit granularity to avoid duplicating visitor-level sums. | Notes on sessions_count uniqueness: sessions_count uses COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, '|', CAST(visitId AS STRING))). Do not assume visitId is globally unique without _TABLE_SUFFIX; any composition that re-partitions or loses _TABLE_SUFFIX context could miscount sessions. When composing, preserve the same session uniqueness logic or recompute sessions_count from session-level data.

views.description: User-level aggregation across sessions (grouped by fullVisitorId) exposing counts and totals per user across the selected shards. Useful for lifetime or period-based user behavior analysis. | Use for: User LTV and behavioral segmentation; Retention cohorts by first_session_date; High-value user identification

views.name: sessions_rank_by_revenue
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  visitId,
  fullVisitorId,
  totals.transactionRevenue AS transaction_revenue,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue,0) DESC, visitStartTime ASC) AS session_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
grain: one row per session with rank within shard (date)

semantic_filters.none: none (downstream may filter by session_rank <= k and/or date range)

params.description: Ranks sessions within each source table shard (by _TABLE_SUFFIX) by transaction revenue, returning one row per session with its rank within that shard (date).
params.when_to_use: Find the highest- or Nth-revenue sessions within a particular GA shard/date (e.g., top-10 sessions by revenue for a given day) | Filter sessions by revenue rank (for sampling, spot-checking, or drilling into top/bottom sessions) before joining to other session- or hit-level data | Compose into aggregations that need revenue-attributed session ranks (for example, count of top-ranked sessions per date) | Build user-facing lists or reports that display session-level revenue and its rank within the date/shard
params.output_schema: table_suffix: the BigQuery table shard name captured by _TABLE_SUFFIX (source: _TABLE_SUFFIX from the source table reference) | session_date: the session date parsed from the string field date in format YYYYMMDD (source: PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) -> date) | visitId: the session-scoped visit/session identifier (source: visitId) | fullVisitorId: the visitor/user identifier (source: fullVisitorId) | transaction_revenue: the session-level transaction revenue as stored in totals.transactionRevenue (source: totals.transactionRevenue) | session_rank: integer rank (ROW_NUMBER) of the session within the same _TABLE_SUFFIX ordered by descending COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue, 0) and tie-broken by ascending visitStartTime (source: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue,0) DESC, visitStartTime ASC))
params.metric: transaction_revenue = totals.transactionRevenue | session_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue, 0) DESC, visitStartTime ASC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-session or one-row-per-key view on (table_suffix, visitId, fullVisitorId) — safe because sessions_rank_by_revenue is one row per session (one row per session with rank within shard), so joining on those keys does not multiply its rows or distort its measures. | Examples of SAFE joins: join to daily_session_aggregates on (table_suffix, visitId, fullVisitorId) if that view is also one-row-per-session; join to user_session_summary on (fullVisitorId) only if user_session_summary is aggregated per user and you intend a user-level expansion (note: joining by fullVisitorId will repeat session rows for multiple user aggregates unless user_session_summary is one-row-per-user and you accept the multiplication). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables/views (unsafe) such as hits_explode or products_explode on (table_suffix, visitId) without re-aggregation, because those explode/normalize views produce multiple rows per session and would duplicate session-level measures (transaction_revenue, session_rank) across the multiple hit/product rows. If you need hit- or product-level detail, either: | - aggregate the hit/product view up to session level first (GROUP BY table_suffix, visitId, fullVisitorId) and then join — this preserves cardinality and prevents duplication of session measures, or | - join and then re-aggregate any session-level metrics (e.g., SUM(transaction_revenue) or MAX(session_rank)) back to session granularity to remove duplication. | When joining to transactions_from_hits or other JOIN-style views that may represent transactions keyed to hits, ensure you join on the exact session keys and then deduplicate or aggregate transaction rows to session-level before combining with this view's session_rank/transaction_revenue to avoid multiplying revenue. | If you need to combine ranks across dates/shards, use table_suffix and/or session_date as join/group keys so the partitioning used to compute session_rank is respected; do not assume session_rank is globally unique across shards without including table_suffix/session_date in the join or filter.

views.description: Ranks sessions within each date (shard) by transaction revenue descending. Exposes a session_rank column so downstream queries can pick top-N per day by filtering on rank. Avoids baking in any specific top-K. | Use for: Top sessions by revenue per day; Sampling highest-value sessions for inspection

views.name: session_running_totals_by_visitor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  visitId,
  visitStartTime,
  totals.pageviews AS pageviews,
  totals.transactions AS transactions,
  SUM(COALESCE(totals.pageviews,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_pageviews,
  SUM(COALESCE(totals.transactions,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_transactions,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime) AS session_number_for_visitor
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
grain: one row per session with per-visitor running totals

semantic_filters.none: none (downstream can restrict to a date/window or visitor subset)

params.description: One row per GA session with per-visitor running totals and session sequence number (cumulative pageviews and transactions by visitor, ordered by session start time).
params.when_to_use: Calculate how many pageviews or transactions a visitor has accumulated up through each session (time series per visitor). | Rank or filter sessions for a visitor by their session order (e.g., analyze the 1st, 2nd, Nth session behavior). | Join session-level metrics to other session-level dimensions (device, traffic source) when you need cumulative counts up to that session. | Build funnel or retention analyses that require an ordering of sessions per visitor and cumulative counts.
params.output_schema: fullVisitorId: unique identifier for the visitor (derived from base column fullVisitorId in ga_sessions_*). | table_suffix: the _TABLE_SUFFIX value from the wildcard table reference (derived from _TABLE_SUFFIX in query), indicates source table partition/date shard. | session_date: session date parsed from the date string (derived from PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) where date is the base column 'date' in ga_sessions_*). | visitId: session identifier within the GA row (derived from base column visitId in ga_sessions_*). | visitStartTime: numeric epoch-like session start time used to order sessions (derived from base column visitStartTime in ga_sessions_*). | pageviews: pageviews count for the session (derived from totals.pageviews in ga_sessions_*). | transactions: transactions count for the session (derived from totals.transactions in ga_sessions_*). | cumulative_pageviews: running sum of session pageviews for this visitor up to and including this session (derived as SUM(COALESCE(totals.pageviews,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)). | cumulative_transactions: running sum of session transactions for this visitor up to and including this session (derived as SUM(COALESCE(totals.transactions,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)). | session_number_for_visitor: session sequence number for the visitor ordered by visitStartTime (derived as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime)).
params.metric: pageviews = totals.pageviews (session-level metric taken directly from totals.pageviews; may be NULL in source; treated as numeric count). | transactions = totals.transactions (session-level metric taken directly from totals.transactions; may be NULL in source; treated as numeric count). | cumulative_pageviews = SUM(COALESCE(totals.pageviews,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) (running total of pageviews per visitor, ordered by visitStartTime). | cumulative_transactions = SUM(COALESCE(totals.transactions,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) (running total of transactions per visitor, ordered by visitStartTime). | session_number_for_visitor = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime) (1-based rank of sessions per visitor by visitStartTime).
params.composition: Safe join: join to session-level or one-row-per-session tables/views on (fullVisitorId, visitId, visitStartTime, session_date) — safe because this view is one row per session, so measures (pageviews, transactions, cumulative_*) will not be duplicated. Example: join to daily_session_aggregates(AGG) on (fullVisitorId, visitId) if that view is one-row-per-session. | Safe join: join to other one-row-per-visitor-per-session views (same grain) on the same keys — safe for preserving metrics. | Unsafe join (do NOT do without re-aggregation): join directly to hit-level or other one-to-many tables/views (e.g., hits_explode(NORM), products_explode(NORM), transactions_from_hits(JOIN)) on fullVisitorId alone or on visitId without aggregating the hit-level rows first — these are one-to-many from session to hits/products and will multiply this view's session-level measures (pageviews, transactions, cumulative_*). | If you must combine with a one-to-many child (hits_explode, products_explode, transactions_from_hits): first aggregate the child to session-level (GROUP BY fullVisitorId, visitId or visitStartTime as appropriate) producing one row per session, then join to this view on the session keys. This preserves correctness of cumulative metrics. | Caveat on ordering key: the running totals and session_number_for_visitor use visitStartTime to order sessions. If you join to another session-like table that has different session start timestamps or multiple session rows per (fullVisitorId, visitId) with different visitStartTime, you must align/resolve to the same ordering key to preserve the intended cumulative semantics. | Partition/table_suffix: table_suffix corresponds to the wildcard table suffix; when composing across date-sharded sources ensure you join on compatible table suffix or session_date to avoid cross-day duplication or mismatched sourcing.

views.description: Per-visitor sessions ordered by visitStartTime with running totals of pageviews and transactions. Useful to compute cumulative behavior across sessions, session-to-session deltas, or to identify N-th session metrics. | Use for: Compute behavior by nth session (e.g., conversion rate on first session); Cumulative LTV-style metrics across sessions

views.name: custom_dimensions_long
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  visitId,
  fullVisitorId,
  cd.index AS cd_index,
  cd.value AS cd_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
UNNEST(customDimensions) AS cd
grain: one row per customDimension entry per session

params.description: Lists every custom dimension entry (index and value) observed for each session, one row per customDimension per session.
params.when_to_use: Report all custom dimension values collected in sessions (e.g., which customDimension indices were set and their values). | Filter or aggregate sessions by specific custom dimension index or value (e.g., count sessions where cd_index = 3 and cd_value = 'X'). | Join custom dimension details into session-level analyses (after ensuring join cardinality is safe) to segment sessions by custom dimensions. | Use as the flattened input when composing further session-level aggregates that depend on custom dimension values (must re-aggregate after joins that can multiply rows).
params.output_schema: table_suffix: source table shard suffix (_TABLE_SUFFIX) from the source ga_sessions_* tables; identifies which per-day table the row came from | session_date: parsed session date (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) from the source 'date' column) representing the session day | visitId: session-level visitId from the source table (visitId) | fullVisitorId: session-level visitor identifier from the source table (fullVisitorId) | cd_index: custom dimension index (cd.index) from the UNNEST(customDimensions) entry | cd_value: custom dimension value (cd.value) from the UNNEST(customDimensions) entry
params.grounded_columns: bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*.date | bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*.visitId | bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*.fullVisitorId | bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*.customDimensions (UNNEST -> cd.index, cd.value) | _TABLE_SUFFIX (implicit BigQuery pseudo-column from ga_sessions_*)
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- number of custom-dimension rows (one per customDimension per session) when aggregated | distinct_sessions = COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(fullVisitorId, '::', CAST(visitId AS STRING), '::', CAST(session_date AS STRING)))  -- count of distinct sessions referenced by these rows | sessions_with_cd = COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(fullVisitorId, '::', CAST(visitId AS STRING), '::', CAST(session_date AS STRING))) FILTER (WHERE cd_index IS NOT NULL)  -- sessions that have at least one custom dimension entry (as represented in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to session-level or one-row-per-session views on (fullVisitorId, visitId, session_date) — safe because this view has at most one row per customDimension per session and therefore joining to a one-row-per-session relation will not duplicate that relation's measures if you aggregate appropriately on the custom-dimension side first or if the target is truly 1:1. | Safe join example: join to daily_session_aggregates (one-row-per-session) ON (fullVisitorId, visitId, session_date) — safe because daily_session_aggregates is one-row-per-session; when you need session-level metrics together with cd_index/cd_value, either (a) keep this view's rows and treat session metrics as repeated for each cd row, or (b) aggregate this view to one-row-per-session first (e.g., array_agg or safe aggregation) to avoid duplication. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many children (e.g., hits_explode, products_explode) without re-aggregation because those views are one-to-many relative to sessions. Joining custom_dimensions_long directly to hits_explode on (fullVisitorId, visitId, session_date) would multiply rows: each combination of a customDimension row and a hit row would produce a separate output row, duplicating session-level measures. | If combining with one-to-many siblings (hits_explode, products_explode, transactions_from_hits), either: (a) perform aggregations on the one-to-many side to produce one-row-per-session before joining, or (b) perform a multi-stage aggregation after the join that divides or groups appropriately so metrics are not double-counted. | Joining to user-level aggregates (e.g., user_session_summary) must consider key granularity: user-level views are one-row-per-user; joining this session-grain view to user-level without aggregation will duplicate user metrics for each session/custom-dimension row. To preserve correct user metrics, aggregate this view up to user level (group by fullVisitorId) before joining, or aggregate the user-level metrics after the join. | Joining on table_suffix is safe for identifying source shard but does not change cardinality semantics — it remains one-row-per-customDimension-per-session. | General rule: treat this view as session-grain but with multiplicity per customDimension. Any join to a relation that is also multi-row per session requires re-aggregation on at least one side before combining session-level measures to avoid multiplying counts/sums.

views.description: Explodes session-level customDimensions array into long form (one row per custom dimension per session). Preserves dimension index and value for pivoting or filtering by custom dimension index/value downstream. | Use for: Pivot custom dimensions into columns for modeling; Filter sessions by custom dimension value

views.name: transactions_from_hits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s._TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) AS session_date,
  s.visitId,
  s.fullVisitorId,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_number,
  hit.transaction.transactionId AS transaction_id,
  hit.transaction.transactionRevenue AS transaction_revenue,
  hit.transaction.transactionTax AS transaction_tax,
  hit.transaction.transactionShipping AS transaction_shipping,
  hit.transaction.currencyCode AS currency_code
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS s,
UNNEST(s.hits) AS hit
WHERE hit.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per hit-level transaction occurrence per session per shard

semantic_filters.hit.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NUL: keeps only hits that include a transaction

params.description: Hit-level rows for hits that contain a transaction: one row per hit-level transaction occurrence per session per shard, exposing transaction identifiers, revenue/tax/shipping and currency along with session keys.
params.when_to_use: List or filter all transactions as recorded on individual hits (e.g., show every hit that recorded a transaction, with hit-level identifiers). | Join to other session- or hit-level data when you need transaction metrics tied to the exact hit that recorded them (for example, attributing a transaction to hit-level dimensions like hitNumber or hit timestamp from the same session). | Compose aggregated transaction metrics (SUM/COUNT) at session, visitor, date, or shard levels by grouping this view — use this view as the atomic rows to aggregate. | Filter transactions by currency_code, date, visitId, fullVisitorId or table_suffix before aggregating or joining to higher-level session/visitor aggregates.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: the _TABLE_SUFFIX value s._TABLE_SUFFIX from the source table; indicates the partition/file shard (original GA dataset suffix) which can be used to identify the source date table. | session_date: PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) — the session date parsed from the base sessions table's date string. | visitId: s.visitId — session-level visit identifier from the sessions table. | fullVisitorId: s.fullVisitorId — visitor identifier from the sessions table. | hit_number: hit.hitNumber — the hit number within the session (hit-level ordinal) from the unnested hits record. | transaction_id: hit.transaction.transactionId — transaction identifier recorded on the hit.transaction structure. | transaction_revenue: hit.transaction.transactionRevenue — transaction revenue value from the hit.transaction structure (note: in GA sample this is typically micros/currency units as provided by the source). | transaction_tax: hit.transaction.transactionTax — transaction tax amount from the hit.transaction structure. | transaction_shipping: hit.transaction.transactionShipping — transaction shipping amount from the hit.transaction structure. | currency_code: hit.transaction.currencyCode — currency code associated with the transaction on the hit.transaction structure.
params.grounded_columns: s._TABLE_SUFFIX | s.date | s.visitId | s.fullVisitorId | s.hits | hit.hitNumber | hit.transaction.transactionId | hit.transaction.transactionRevenue | hit.transaction.transactionTax | hit.transaction.transactionShipping | hit.transaction.currencyCode
params.metric: transaction_revenue = hit.transaction.transactionRevenue  (use SUM(transaction_revenue) when aggregating over multiple rows to get total revenue) | transaction_tax = hit.transaction.transactionTax  (use SUM(transaction_tax) when aggregating) | transaction_shipping = hit.transaction.transactionShipping  (use SUM(transaction_shipping) when aggregating) | transaction_count = COUNT(*)  when counting transaction occurrences in this view (each row = one hit-level transaction occurrence)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to session- or visitor-level one-row-per-session or one-row-per-visitor views/tables on (table_suffix, session_date, visitId, fullVisitorId) — safe because this view is one row per hit-level transaction occurrence and those session/visitor views are one-row-per-session or one-row-per-visitor, so session/visitor measures will not be duplicated when joining to this view (the hit-level rows naturally expand the session/visitor row as intended). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hits_explode (NORM) on (table_suffix, session_date, visitId, fullVisitorId, hit_number) — safe for enrichments that are strictly one-to-one at the hit level, because both are derived from the same s.hits element keyed by hitNumber; measures from this view remain aligned and not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to products_explode (NORM) without re-aggregation: products_explode is one-to-many per hit (multiple product rows per hit). Joining transactions_from_hits to products_explode on hit keys will multiply transaction_revenue/transaction amounts by the number of products per hit. If you need product-level attribution, first aggregate or distribute transaction metrics appropriately (for example, allocate revenue across products or aggregate transactions_from_hits to hit-level counts before joining). | do NOT join to sibling AGG views (daily_session_aggregates, user_session_summary) on session or visitor keys expecting those AGG metrics to remain unique unless you understand their grain: AGG views are one-row-per-session or one-row-per-visitor — joining them to this hit-level transactional view is acceptable if you expect hit-level expansion of session/visitor aggregates, but avoid joining back and forth to other one-to-many tables which would multiply rows without re-aggregation. | when composing further aggregations: to produce stable aggregated metrics (e.g., total revenue per session or per user), GROUP BY the desired grain and use SUM(transaction_revenue), SUM(transaction_tax), SUM(transaction_shipping) and COUNT(*) for transaction occurrences; do not rely on joining to other one-to-many expansions without first reducing them to the target grain.

views.description: Flattened transaction-level rows derived from hits.transaction fields. Exposes transactionId, revenue and session keys; use this to aggregate transactions avoiding double-count when products are also unnested. | Use for: Transaction-level revenue rollups and deduplication; Mapping transactions to sessions and channels
